request.query: Which passages state the same fact as either of these two statements? (1) A `fasthttp.Client` given to [NewWithClient](./rest.md#newwithclient) may have served hosts already and Fiber cannot tell, so it counts only when it was created with `DisablePathNormalizing: true`. (2) It does not read the setting of a fasthttp client that was created with `DisablePathNormalizing: true`. ```go title="Signature" func (c *Client) DisablePathNormalizing() bool ```
request.instructions: A passage answers only if it itself states the fact that the two statements disagree about: a value, version, limit, name, list or rule for the same thing. A passage that only mentions the topic does not answer.

documents.title: docs/client/rest.md > Usage > NewWithClient
documents.text:
### NewWithClient

**NewWithClient** creates and returns a new Client object from an existing `fasthttp.Client`. It panics if `c` is `nil`.

Fiber cannot tell whether that client has served a host already. Unless it was created with `DisablePathNormalizing: true`, [SetDisablePathNormalizing](#setdisablepathnormalizing) changes what is sent to hosts it has not served yet, but the check that keeps a path parameter value inside its segment stays on.

```go title="Signature"
func NewWithClient(c *fasthttp.Client) *Client
```

documents.title: docs/client/rest.md > Path Normalizing > SetDisablePathNormalizing
documents.text:
### SetDisablePathNormalizing

Turns path normalizing off or on for every request of the client. It is on by default: the request path is normalized before it is sent, which decodes percent-escapes, collapses `//` and resolves `.` and `..` segments, so `/a//b/./c%2Fd` goes out as `/a/b/c/d`. With normalizing off, the path is sent as written. fasthttp normalizes the path when it writes the request, according to the client that sends it, so the setting is applied to the `DisablePathNormalizing` field of the wrapped fasthttp client, and of every host client behind a load balancer: a client created with [NewWithClient](#newwithclient), [NewWithHostClient](#newwithhostclient) or [NewWithLBClient](#newwithlbclient) changes the fasthttp client it wraps, for everyone who shares it. Call it before the first request, because a `fasthttp.Client` copies the setting into each host client when it first creates it, and a host it already serves keeps normalizing until fasthttp drops its entry, see the note under [TLS](#tls) for when. Fiber keeps rejecting path parameter values that would leave their segment unless it knows that the path is sent as built. It knows for a client from `New`, until a request has gone out through it while it normalized; for a client from `NewWithHostClient`, which reads the field on every request; for a client from `NewWithLBClient` whose host clients all have the field on; and for a `fasthttp.Client` given to `NewWithClient` that was created with `DisablePathNormalizing: true`. A `fasthttp.Client` given to `NewWithClient` without it may have served hosts already, so Fiber cannot tell and keeps the check on, although hosts it has not served yet get the setting. A balancer that holds a client that is neither a `*fasthttp.HostClient` nor a wrapper exposing a nested balancer through `LBClient()` cannot be told either and counts as normalizing. A request skips Fiber's normalizing when either the client or the request disables it; see [SetDisablePathNormalizing](./request.md#setdisablepathnormalizing) for the request-level setting.

```go title="Signature"
func (c *Client) SetDisablePathNormalizing(disable bool) *Client
```

documents.title: docs/client/request.md > SetDisablePathNormalizing
documents.text:
## SetDisablePathNormalizing

**SetDisablePathNormalizing** turns path normalizing off or on for the request. It is on by default: the request path is normalized before it is sent, which decodes percent-escapes, collapses `//` and resolves `.` and `..` segments, so `/a//b/./c%2Fd` goes out as `/a/b/c/d`. With normalizing off, Fiber builds the URL without normalizing it. Whether the path is normalized again when the request is written is up to the wrapped fasthttp client, which a single request cannot change: the path goes out as written only when the client has normalizing turned off, with [SetDisablePathNormalizing](./rest.md#setdisablepathnormalizing) on the client or with a fasthttp client created with `DisablePathNormalizing: true` (see [NewWithClient](./rest.md#newwithclient)). On any other client this setting changes neither what is sent nor the path parameter check. Path parameter values are checked differently while normalizing is off, as described under [SetPathParam](#setpathparam).

```go title="Signature"
func (r *Request) SetDisablePathNormalizing(disable bool) *Request
```

documents.title: docs/client/request.md > DisablePathNormalizing
documents.text:
## DisablePathNormalizing

**DisablePathNormalizing** reports whether path normalizing is disabled for this request. It does not reflect the client's setting; Fiber builds the URL without normalizing it when either one disables it, see [SetDisablePathNormalizing](#setdisablepathnormalizing) for what reaches the wire.

```go title="Signature"
func (r *Request) DisablePathNormalizing() bool
```

documents.title: docs/whats_new.md > 🌎 Client package > Configuration improvements
documents.text:
### Configuration improvements

The v3 client centralizes common configuration on the client instance and lets you override it per request with `client.Config`.
You can define base URLs, defaults (headers, cookies, path parameters, timeouts), and toggle path normalization once, while still
using axios-style helpers for each call.

```go
cc := client.New().
    SetBaseURL("https://api.service.local").
    AddHeader("Authorization", "Bearer <token>").
    SetTimeout(5 * time.Second).
    SetPathParam("tenant", "acme").
    SetDisablePathNormalizing(true)

resp, err := cc.Get("/users/:tenant/:id", client.Config{
    PathParam: map[string]string{"id": "42"},
    Param:     map[string]string{"include": "profile"},
})
if err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
defer resp.Close()
fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode(), resp.String())
```

:::caution
A path parameter value now fills exactly one path segment. A value holding `/`
or `\`, a value that is exactly `.` or `..`, an empty value, and one of those
followed by `;` parameters, such as `..;`, are rejected with
`ErrPathParamInPath`; a value substituted into the host must already be a
valid host or the request fails with `ErrPathParamInHost`. Previously such a
value was pasted in unchanged, so `SetPathParam("id", "../../admin")` on
`/api/:id` quietly sent the request to `/admin`. Call
`SetDisablePathNormalizing(true)` on the client to send a multi-segment value on
purpose (for a client from `NewWithClient`, create the fasthttp client with
`DisablePathNormalizing: true` as well); the setting on a single request only
counts for a client that already sends paths as written. `.`, `..` and an empty
value stay rejected either way, with or without `;` parameters, because a server
resolves a dot segment and may merge slashes.
:::

:::note
`Debug()` logs the raw request and response after each response through the
client's logger, which is Fiber's default logger unless `SetLogger` chose
another one. The text is logged as it is, `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers
and bodies included. A request with no referer set carries no `Referer` header;
it used to carry an empty one.
:::

documents.title: docs/client/rest.md > TLS > SetRootCertificate
documents.text:
### SetRootCertificate

Adds one or more root certificates from a PEM file to the `RootCAs` pool of the client's TLS configuration. A new client has no pool (`RootCAs` is `nil`, which means the system roots), so the first call creates one that holds only the given certificates: they replace the system roots instead of being added to them, and later calls add to that pool. If the configuration already has a `RootCAs` pool, for example one built from `x509.SystemCertPool()` and set with [SetTLSConfig](#settlsconfig), the certificates are appended to that pool, and they reach a host the client already uses; the call that creates the pool does not, see the note under [TLS](#tls). To keep trusting the system roots, build the pool that way, as in the [TLS example](./examples.md#tls). It panics if the file cannot be read or holds no valid PEM certificate.

```go title="Signature"
func (c *Client) SetRootCertificate(path string) *Client
```

docs/client/request.md > SetContext
documents.text:
## SetContext

**SetContext** sets the `context.Context` for the request, allowing you to cancel or time out the request. See the [Go blog](https://blog.golang.org/context) and [context](https://pkg.go.dev/context) docs for more details.

A deadline bounds the exchange at the transport. A cancellation ends it on a client from `client.New` as well: the connection the request was using is closed, so neither the goroutine nor the connection outlives the call once the connection is open. A cancellation while the client is still dialing, or waiting for a free connection, takes effect when the dial or the wait ends, and the connection it produced is then closed unused: the built-in dialer gives up after 3 seconds, a dialer set with `SetDial` or `SetProxyURL` bounds itself. With `SetStreamResponseBody(true)` a cancellation does not reach the transport: the caller returns at once, the exchange waits for the server or the client's timeouts, and a body already being streamed ends when it is closed. A timeout or deadline does reach it, since the connection takes it as its read and write deadline, so give a streamed request one (`SetTimeout`, or a context with a deadline): a server that never answers then leaves no goroutine or connection behind once it passes. A wrapped `fasthttp` client (`NewWithClient`, `NewWithHostClient`, `NewWithLBClient`) returns the caller at once while its exchange ends on its own, when the server answers or the client's own timeouts pass, so give such a client `ReadTimeout` and `WriteTimeout`.

```go title="Signature"
func (r *Request) SetContext(ctx context.Context) *Request
```

documents.text:
#### Config fields

| Property                                                                | Type                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Default            |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| <Reference id="beforeservefunc">BeforeServeFunc</Reference>             | `func(app *App) error`        | Allows customizing and accessing fiber app before serving the app. If it returns an error, `Listen` and `Listener` return that error without serving, and `Listen` closes the listener it created. It is not called when `EnablePrefork` is enabled.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `nil`              |
| <Reference id="certclientfile">CertClientFile</Reference>               | `string`                      | Path of the CA bundle used to verify client certificates, for mTLS on the `CertFile`/`CertKeyFile` path. Ignored when `TLSConfig` is set: that config is served as supplied and this field does not modify it, so a client certificate is required only if its `ClientAuth` is a Require mode, verified against its `ClientCAs`. Fiber logs a warning when both are supplied.             | `""`               |
| <Reference id="certfile">CertFile</Reference>                           | `string`                      | Path of the certificate file. If you want to use TLS, you must enter this field together with `CertKeyFile`; setting only one of them makes `Listen` return `fiber.ErrCertFileAndKeyRequired` instead of silently serving plaintext HTTP.                                                                                    | `""`               |
| <Reference id="certkeyfile">CertKeyFile</Reference>                     | `string`                      | Path of the certificate's private key. If you want to use TLS, you must enter this field together with `CertFile`.                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `""`               |
| <Reference id="disablestartupmessage">DisableStartupMessage</Reference> | `bool`                        | When set to true, it will not print out the «Fiber» ASCII art and listening address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `false`            |
| <Reference id="enableprefork">EnablePrefork</Reference>                 | `bool`                        | When set to true, this will spawn multiple Go processes listening on the same port.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `false`            |
